messages.text: This is terminal ileum: stem cells and Paneth cells sit at the crypt bases.

Terminal ileum (your words). Your Paneth cells are hidden inside 'Stem cells': a sub-cluster of 544 crypt-base cells (25% of the stem cells) has ITLN2 in 94%, plus KLK12 and GUCA2A, while ITLN2 is in 3% of the other epithelial cells. The current Paneth markers (ITLN1, SPINK4) mark goblet cells, so no Paneth cells were found. I set them to ITLN2/KLK12/SEC11C. Stem cells and TAs do sit at the crypt base (next to TAs, EEC and tuft cells; closer to the muscle than enterocytes), so SI-03 holds. Images: the overview shows villi and crypts at the top (rows A–J), a thick loose submucosa with large vessels (L–T) and the muscularis propria (U–AA). Zoomed in, the epithelium (H6:J10) fits the crypts on the H&E. The submucosa (R4:V12) is full of 'Crypt-bottom fibroblasts' (median 841 µm from the epithelium). They are GREM1+ SFRP2+ OGN+ submucosal fibroblasts, not crypt-bottom ones, so I rename them by their markers. One of their sub-clusters (948 cells, DES 92%, MYH11 95%) lies in the muscularis propria and is smooth muscle (optional). Other changes: weak or unspecific markers swapped for the ones the data separate (Cycling TAs, Enterocytes, Goblet, Effector/memory CD4, telocytes, ILCs, pericytes). Most 'NK cells' are TRDC+ gd T cells (TRDC 56% vs 3%; CD3E 48%), as SI-08 expects. M cells, eosinophils, FDCs and monocytes are not found: the panel detects their markers in very few cells (e.g. CCL23 in 9 cells, CLC in 5).
? M cells, eosinophils, follicular dendritic cells and monocytes are not found (CCL23 in 9 cells, CLC in 5, FDCSP in 168). Should they stay in the list or be removed?
? Effector/memory CD4 sub-cluster /1 (220 cells, 1.1 mm deep in the submucosa) carries fibroblast genes (SFRP2, GREM1, C3): are there T-cell infiltrates in the submucosa (diverticulitis), or should these count as fibroblasts?

edits.problem: Paneth cells hidden in Stem cells
edits.reason: ITLN1 and SPINK4 are goblet markers here (ITLN1 in 87% of goblet cells), so the Paneth type never got a cluster. Stem-cell sub-cluster /2 (544 cells at the crypt base) has ITLN2 94% (vs 45% in the other stem cells, 3% in the rest of the epithelium), KLK12 48% vs 6%, SEC11C 76% vs 33%. ITLN2 is Paneth-specific (Nonnecke 2022). You said Paneth cells sit at the crypt bases.
edits.evidence: type_structure Stem cells /2: ITLN2 0.94 vs 0.45, KLK12 0.48 vs 0.06, SEC11C 0.76 vs 0.33, GUCA2A 0.52 vs 0.06; review_markers Stem cells: ITLN2 0.57 vs 0.03 in sibling epithelial types. KLK12/SEC11C shares outside the stem cells not checked.
edits.group: Paneth cells hidden in Stem cells

edits.problem: Paneth cells hidden in Stem cells
edits.reason: SPDEF is detected in 8% of goblet cells; ITLN1 and REP15 mark them here. ITLN1 moved here from Paneth.
edits.evidence: review_markers Goblet: SPDEF 0.08 vs 0.01 (weak), ITLN1 0.87 vs 0.34, REP15 0.6 vs 0.13, SPINK4 0.78 vs 0.26
edits.group: Paneth cells hidden in Stem cells

edits.reason: PCLAF and UBE2C are detected in few cycling cells; RRM2 and TYMS are detected in about half.
edits.evidence: PCLAF 0.13, UBE2C 0.19 (weak); RRM2 0.52 vs 0.05, TYMS 0.46 vs 0.05

edits.reason: FABP2 is in 70% of the other epithelial cells, so it does not separate enterocytes; SLC26A3 does.
edits.evidence: FABP2 0.9 vs 0.7 (not specific); SLC26A3 0.54 vs 0.08, APOB 0.85 vs 0.13

edits.reason: These cells lie in the submucosa and around the muscle (median 841 µm from the epithelium, 60 µm from the muscle), not at the crypt bottoms. Named by their markers.
edits.evidence: spatial_profile: distance to epithelium q 293/841/1756 µm; show_area R4:V12: they fill the loose submucosa; GREM1 0.69 vs 0.02, SFRP2 0.59 vs 0.01, OGN 0.6 vs 0.01

edits.reason: SFRP2 and OGN separate them from the telocytes better than SOX6- does; SOX6 is hardly detected.
edits.evidence: SFRP2 0.59 vs 0.01, OGN 0.6 vs 0.01; SOX6 in 0.01 of these, 0.18 of telocytes

edits.reason: SOX6 and WNT5A are detected in few telocytes; EDNRB separates them from the other fibroblasts.

edits.question: Should the DES+ MYH11+ cells in the muscularis propria now under the fibroblasts go back to smooth muscle (which also makes PDGFRA+ interstitial cells of the muscle count as smooth muscle)?
edits.reason: Sub-cluster /1 of the GREM1+ fibroblasts (948 cells) is in the muscularis propria and expresses smooth muscle genes; PDGFRA spill-over between packed muscle cells pushes them out of smooth muscle.
edits.evidence: type_structure /1: DES 0.92 vs 0.2, MYH11 0.95 vs 0.31, ACTG2 0.87 vs 0.28, depth median 2307 µm; Fibroblasts MYH11- flagged (0.36)
